Definition: a ram (just old enough to butt)
BiblicalUsage: Kebes means a lamb, a young ram: Leviticus 23:12 says ye shall offer an he lamb without blemish for a burnt offering unto the LORD. Numbers 15:11 sets the rule for one bullock, or one ram, or for a lamb, or a kid. 1 Chronicles 29:21 says they offered a thousand lambs with their drink offerings for all Israel. Proverbs 27:26 says the lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lamb runs through the whole Bible: offered without blemish, counted by the thousand, and worn as clothing. I hold that every lamb on those altars was pointing to the one Lamb who would take away the sin of the world.
